about: The Phase 5.3-5.4 thresholds. scripts/panel.py and scripts/check_gate.py read this file and nothing else for them; SKILL.md 5.4 and consensus-protocol.md point here. Scores are on each dimension's rubric scale; overall_score and target_score are 0..1. max_panel_rounds caps the panel rounds (a consensus over a new skill hash) on the panel-verdict path; each round re-scores every dimension. gold_gate caps the verdict on both paths, by caveat_margin. metric_first replaces the panel's verdict when rubric.yaml says `metric: answer-key`. max_fix_cycles and fix_cycle: scripts/fix_cycle.py. hooks/finish_guard.py reads max_finish_sendbacks: the finish guard's send-backs per build, after which a stop ends it unfinished. lite holds the small-builder profile's numbers (scripts read it when work/manifest.yaml says `profile: lite` or CSA_PROFILE=lite): runs_per_arm per gate arm, the Phase 4 caps, the one-reviewer panel's round cap and rescores per skill commit; the full profile ignores it.
fix_cycle: after the panel's round, on cited findings (a receipt's veto, or a failure scenario with evidence and repro) whatever the consensus label, up to max_fix_cycles cycles on every profile: one commit fixing only the cited lines (or adopting a change already made), rescore.py and the gate on it, then each role that raised a finding re-checks it (references/panel/recheck.md). --next pushes a cycle only for a blocking finding (a metric-first veto; any finding under ITERATE, BLOCK or ESCALATE) or a change to adopt; the freeze guard names the command for the rest. The verdict never rises above the original consensus: metric-first, the gate and metric levels decide; panel-verdict path, SHIP and SHIP WITH CAVEATS keep their cap and ITERATE, BLOCK or ESCALATE cap at SHIP WITH CAVEATS. Resolved findings only lift vetoes: an unresolved blocking finding or a re-check's regression keeps UNSHIPPED (the next cycle, or the end); an unresolved plain finding changes nothing. Not opened when the gate or metric is already at UNSHIPPED; never re-runs the panel

labels.ESCALATE: a deadlocked dimension after synthesis, or the Devil's Advocate's ESCALATE: the user decides; terminal label UNSHIPPED
labels.BLOCK: block_majority or more members score a dimension below block_below: terminal label UNSHIPPED unless Phase 4 fixes it
labels.SHIP: overall_score >= target_score and no dimension blocked
labels.ITERATE: overall_score < target_score - caveat_margin: back to Phase 4, or UNSHIPPED with no budget left

gold_gate: the 5.0 gold deltas allow SHIP when every one is > 0, at most SHIP WITH CAVEATS when the lowest is >= -caveat_margin, else only UNSHIPPED; on the panel path as on metric_first

metric_first.applies_when: work/evaluation/rubric.yaml has `metric: answer-key` (phase-3.md 3.4); absent or `metric: llm-judge` keeps the panel's verdict (labels, allowed_terminal)
metric_first.metric: the last kept autoresearch.jsonl experiment whose commit output/<skill>/ still matches: the lower of its metric and its held_out (phase-4.md 4.2: the validation, synthetic or leave-one-out case it was not tuned on), never the training metric alone; no numeric held_out is no metric (UNSHIPPED). The 3.5 fast path and the 4.3 loop stops read held_out too
metric_first.gate: gold_gate (a valid gate already passed every trigger and near-miss indicator)
metric_first.metric_level: SHIP at >= target_score; SHIP WITH CAVEATS at >= target_score - caveat_margin; else UNSHIPPED
metric_first.allowed: the lower of the gate's and the metric's level; UNSHIPPED on any panel veto

veto_kinds.hard_constraint: a phase-3.md 3.3 hard constraint the skill breaks
veto_kinds.safety: fetched content followed as instructions, a destructive command, or a like safety defect
veto_kinds.escalate: the Devil's Advocate's ESCALATE, with a cited quote and a reproducible failure

lite.applies_when: work/manifest.yaml `profile: lite` (check_gate.py --next --profile lite) or CSA_PROFILE=lite, which wins
lite.runs_why: the fewest runs that still give each arm a spread (never 1); r19: all 60 gates reach the same gold-delta level on their first 2 runs per arm as on 3, median per-arm stdev 0.000
lite.loop_why: caps on rubric.yaml's values (the lower wins); r18+r19 Haiku: 9 of 122 Phase 4 experiments raised the best held-out score, 8 of them by experiment 3; plateau_window 1 would have dropped 2 of the 5 still reached
lite.panel_why: one reviewer (quality, utility and adversarial in references/panel/reviewer.md), no synthesis round; metric_first keeps its 1 round, the panel-verdict path allows one ITERATE
